issues.description: play.ts changed to import from local source path and contains scratch debugging code
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from './packages/zod/src/index.js' and contains console.log debugging output for the two reported cases. This appears to be developer scratch work that should not land. At minimum it needs to be reverted to the prior placeholder; ideally the two cases would be promoted to actual test assertions in to-json-schema.test.ts since they reflect the bug being fixed.

issues.description: overrideCount jumped from 6 to 12 with only the snapshot expectation updated and no justification
issues.detail: In to-json-schema.test.ts the assertion `expect(overrideCount).toBe(6)` was changed to `toBe(12)`. The previous behavior intentionally skipped overrides on parent nodes (`if (!seen.isParent)`), and that guard has been removed in finalize(). Doubling the number of override invocations is a user-visible behavior change for anyone passing a custom `override` callback — every refinement chain link (parent + child) will now fire the override. This needs an explicit design decision and changelog note, not a silent snapshot bump.

issues.description: Removal of `if (!seen.isParent)` guard changes override semantics for all consumers
issues.detail: to-json-schema.ts previously suppressed `ctx.override(...)` calls on parent (cloned-from) nodes. This PR removes that guard unconditionally. Even setting aside the doubled count in the test, this means consumers who relied on overrides only running on the user-visible schema will now see overrides also running on the underlying parent. This is a breaking semantic change that warrants either preserving the prior behavior or explicit documentation.

issues.description: Deep-equality via JSON.stringify is fragile and O(n) per key
issues.detail: Both new de-duplication blocks use `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])` to decide whether to delete a property. JSON.stringify is non-deterministic for key order on objects (insertion order matters), throws on cycles, and silently mishandles undefined/functions/BigInt. For nested schema properties this can either false-negative (leaving redundant copies) or false-positive (deleting intentionally divergent values). A structural deep-equal helper would be safer; at minimum, document why stringify is sufficient here.

issues.description: Recursive flattenRef on seen.parent may double-process and is order-sensitive
issues.detail: After the main `if (ref) { ... }` block, the new code calls `flattenRef(seen.parent)` again when `seen.parent !== ref`. Because `seen.ref` of the parent may have already been nulled in a prior pass, the parent's def may or may not have inherited properties depending on outer iteration order. The finalize loop iterates `[...ctx.seen.entries()].reverse()` and relies on this implicit ordering — any change to insertion order in `process()` could silently change emitted JSON schemas. This warrants an explicit ordering invariant comment and ideally a test for nested wrapper chains (e.g. readonly().nullable().meta({id}).describe()).

issues.description: z.file() snapshot change moves shared props out of anyOf branches — spec compliance unclear
issues.detail: fileProcessor previously emitted each mime branch as a complete StringSchema inside anyOf. Now shared props (contentEncoding, format, maxLength, minLength, type) live at the root and anyOf branches contain only `{ contentMediaType }`. While arguably DRYer, JSON Schema validators applying anyOf semantics will validate each subschema independently; bare `{ contentMediaType: 'image/png' }` is a no-op schema (contentMediaType is annotation-only in most drafts), so the effective constraint shifts. Confirm this still validates the same set of instances across draft-07, 2020-12, and openapi-3.0 targets, and add a regression test asserting validation behavior, not just shape.

issues.description: isParentRef check uses `(zodSchema as any)._zod.parent === ref` and assumes identity
issues.detail: The new branch distinguishes parent-chain refs from processor-set refs via `_zod.parent === ref`. This couples finalize() tightly to the exact identity set in process(). If any code path mutates or reassigns `_zod.parent`, the parent-only-property pruning will silently regress. Consider stashing this as an explicit boolean on `Seen` at process time (e.g., `seen.refIsParent`) rather than re-deriving it.

issues.description: ZodType.check now sets `{ parent: true }` while ZodMiniType comment was just uncommented
issues.detail: The mini change is reverting a previously commented-out option. Worth a brief note in CHANGELOG explaining that both classic and mini `check()` now establish parent linkage for metadata propagation, since downstream users who relied on the old behavior (no parent link, no metadata inheritance through check chains) may see different JSON schema output.

issues.description: New test asserts shape but not the underlying bug condition
issues.detail: `test("describe with id on wrapper")` exercises readonly + id + describe and asserts via inline snapshot. The test docstring mentions the processor-vs-parent ref divergence, but the assertion only checks output shape. A direct assertion that both `current.$ref` and `previous.$ref` point to `#/$defs/roJobId` would survive snapshot-bumping refactors and document intent.

issues.description: Seen.ref type narrowed from `T | undefined | null` to `T | null` — loses `undefined`
issues.detail: Previously `ref?: schemas.$ZodType | undefined | null`, now `ref?: schemas.$ZodType | null`. The `?` already implies undefined, so this is mostly cosmetic, but combined with the new sentinel `seen.ref === null` (meaning 'already processed') it's worth a one-line comment explaining the three states: undefined (never set), null (processed/cleared), $ZodType (pending flatten).

dissents.topic: Whether removing the `if (!seen.isParent)` override guard is a bug fix or a breaking change

positions.position: The previous guard was wrong: parent nodes in the seen map represent real JSON schema fragments the user can observe in $defs, and skipping override() on them was inconsistent. Doubling the count to 12 reflects the correct semantics.

This is a breaking change for anyone using a custom override callback to mutate JSON schema once per logical schema. The PR description does not flag it, and downstream tools (OpenAPI generators, doc tools) may now receive override calls they didn't expect. Even if correct, it needs a deprecation path or changelog note.

dissents.topic: Whether de-duplication via JSON.stringify is acceptable

positions.position: JSON Schema values are JSON-serializable by definition, and within a single finalize pass key order is stable because both sides come from the same processor. Stringify-equality is fine and avoids dragging in a deep-equal dependency.

Object key order from Object.assign + later property additions is not guaranteed equal across the child's copy and the parent's def, particularly after future processor changes. A structural compare is one small helper and removes a class of silent regressions.

dissents.topic: Whether the z.file() anyOf restructuring is in scope for this PR

positions.position: The PR is titled 'metadata tracking across child-parent relationships'. Restructuring fileProcessor output is an unrelated cleanup that should ship in a separate PR with its own validation-equivalence rationale.

The fileProcessor change is a direct consequence of the new inheritance model — shared properties at the root now propagate sensibly via the parent chain, so factoring them out is the natural expression of the same fix.

review.summary: The PR's core idea — tracking a `parent` link separately from the processor-set `ref` so $ref propagation survives wrappers like `readonly().meta({id}).describe()` — is sound and the new test case captures the intended fix. However, the change ships with two collateral edits that need attention: (1) `play.ts` was modified into a local scratch file with console.log debugging and should be reverted or its cases promoted to tests; (2) the `if (!seen.isParent)` override guard was removed, silently doubling `override` callback invocations (6 → 12 in the existing test) which is a breaking semantic change for consumers with custom overrides. Secondary concerns: JSON.stringify is used as a deep-equality oracle for property de-duplication (fragile for nested values), the `_zod.parent === ref` identity check should be precomputed and stored on Seen, and the z.file() anyOf restructuring is scope-creep that needs its own validation-equivalence rationale. The new test should also assert `$ref` directly rather than relying solely on an inline snapshot.
